what: When a break proved by a whole check (for example the unit check) runs past its two-minute limit, or the owner presses Ctrl+C during that run, python3 prove.py ends but the check it started keeps running in the background, along with anything that check started (a test run, a browser, a served app); the spec says each run never outlives the command. The cause is that prove.py stops a run by sending SIGKILL to the process group of `checks.py <name>`, and checks.py starts each check in a new session of its own, so checks.py is killed before its own clean-up can stop the check, and the check is out of reach of the kill. The test of the time limit only uses a break proved by a single test, which runs in prove.py's own group, so it cannot see this; the demonstration script is red because the check's pytest is still alive after the proof ended.

A later build can silence the linter on any line with a bare `# noqa` (no rule named and no reason given), and every check stays green: Ruff reports nothing for that line and every test in tests/test_lint.py still passes. The spec allows only a `# noqa` that names the one rule it silences, with the reason on the same line, and forbids a blanket one. The cause is that the selected rules do not include one that rejects a bare `# noqa`, and the tests that hold "exempts nothing" look only at Ruff's config files and at file-level `# ruff: noqa` lines, never at line-level markers; a marker that names a rule but gives no reason is not held either.

CLAUDE.md, the first file every agent reads, still says that python3 checks.py runs "every check (the pattern rules, the defect log, the unit suite, the browser walks)": four checks, with the new linter missing. The spec asks that every sentence listing the checks agree with the code, and ticket 03 reported that no such sentence was left. The cause is that ticket 03 searched for the words "four checks" and for the checks' code names, and this sentence uses neither, so it was missed; no test holds it to CHECKS.
